verses.text: Jericho was locked down tight because of the Israelites. Nobody went out or came in.
The LORD told Joshua, “Look, I've handed Jericho over to you, along with its king and its best fighters.
All your fighting men are to march around the city once a day for six days.
Seven priests will carry seven ram's-horn trumpets ahead of the ark. On the seventh day you'll march around the city seven times, and the priests will blow the trumpets.
When you hear one long blast from the ram's horn, everyone must shout as loudly as they can. The city wall will collapse, and everyone can go straight in from where they're standing.”
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said, “Pick up the ark of the covenant, and have seven priests carry seven ram's-horn trumpets ahead of the LORD's ark.”
They told the people, “Move out! March around the city, with the armed men going ahead of the LORD's ark.”
After Joshua spoke, the seven priests went ahead of the LORD, blowing their seven ram's-horn trumpets, and the ark of the LORD's covenant went behind them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark. The trumpets kept sounding as they went.
Joshua told the people, “Don't shout, don't raise your voice, and don't say a word until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout.”
So Joshua had the LORD's ark carried once around the city. Then everyone went back to camp and stayed there.
Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests picked up the LORD's ark.

The seven priests carrying the seven ram's horns went ahead of the LORD's ark and kept blowing the trumpets as they marched. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the LORD's ark. The horns kept sounding as they went.
On the second day they went around the city once, then went back to camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they got up at dawn and marched around the city the same way, but seven times. That was the only day they went around seven times.
On the seventh trip around, the priests blew the trumpets and Joshua told the people, “Shout! The LORD has given you the city!
The city and everything in it are set apart for the LORD. Only Rahab the sex worker and those with her in her house will live, because she hid the messengers we sent.
Stay away from anything set apart for destruction. If you take any of it for yourselves after setting it apart, you'll bring a curse and trouble on Israel's camp.
All the silver, gold, and objects made of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD. They go into the LORD's treasury.”
The priests blew the trumpets, and when the people heard the blast, they let out a mighty shout. The wall collapsed, everyone went straight into the city from where they stood, and they took it.
They put everything in the city to the sword, men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
Joshua told the two men who had scouted the land, “Go into the woman's house and bring her and everyone who belongs to her out, as you swore to her.”
The two young scouts went in and brought Rahab out with her father, mother, brothers, and everyone who belonged to her. They brought out all her relatives and settled them outside Israel's camp.
They burned the city and everything in it. They put the silver, gold, and objects of bronze and iron in the treasury of the LORD's house.
Joshua spared Rahab the sex worker, her father's household, and everyone with her. She lives among the Israelites to this day because she hid the messengers Joshua sent to scout Jericho.

Then Joshua made the people take an oath: “Anyone who sets out to rebuild Jericho is cursed before the LORD. Laying its foundation will cost him his firstborn. Setting up its gates will cost him his youngest son.”
The LORD was with Joshua, and word about him spread across the entire land.
